subject: paediatrics
title: Chronic respiratory disorders: asthma cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis

steps.tx: **Asthma** causes episodic wheeze that worsens at night, with exercise and with laughing. Triggers include viral infections, dust, smoke and pets, and atopy shows as eczema, rhinitis or family history. Spirometry shows **reversible obstruction** when it can be performed reliably by the child. Reliever therapy uses a short acting bronchodilator as needed, controller therapy uses daily inhaled corticosteroid in steps, and spacer technique is checked with a written action plan.
steps.say: Asthma causes episodic wheeze that worsens at night. Viral infections and dust are commonly triggering acute symptoms. Spirometry is showing obstruction that is reversing with bronchodilator therapy. Written action plans help families manage worsening symptoms.

steps.tx: **Cystic fibrosis** presents in newborns with meconium ileus and is screened at birth in many programmes. The **sweat chloride test** confirms the diagnosis, pancreatic insufficiency causes steatorrhoea needing enzymes, and Pseudomonas colonises damaged lungs. Liver disease, cystic fibrosis related diabetes screened by oral glucose tolerance testing, and F508del modulator therapy complete the picture. Physiotherapy clears airways, dietitians support high energy intake, and heat causes extra salt losses.
steps.say: Cystic fibrosis blocks ducts in lungs, pancreas and bowel. The sweat chloride test confirms the diagnosis reliably. Pancreatic enzymes replace what the blocked gland cannot deliver. Physiotherapy and nutrition support growth and lung health.

steps.tx: This diagram traces one **CFTR chloride channel defect** to disease in several organs at once. Dehydrated airway fluid leaves bronchi plugged with thick purulent mucus, the sweat gland loses excess chloride, and blocked pancreatic ducts cause steatorrhoea. The newborn bowel obstructs with **meconium ileus**, which may be the first presentation. The picture matters because one channel defect explains why lung, pancreas, bowel and sweat findings belong together in a stem.
steps.say: This diagram shows how one defective chloride channel affects many organs. Thick mucus is plugging the bronchi and is impairing clearance. Blocked pancreatic ducts cause fatty stools and poor growth. Meconium ileus is obstructing the bowel in newborn babies.

vis.alt: Airway, sweat gland, pancreas and bowel diagrams showing plugged bronchi, blocked ducts and ileus.
vis.caption: CFTR defect with plugged bronchi, pancreatic and bowel disease. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Bronchiectasis** causes a chronic wet productive cough that persists despite usual treatment. High resolution CT confirms the diagnosis with the **signet ring sign** and tramline thickening of bronchial walls. Causes include post tuberculous damage, immunodeficiency and primary ciliary dyskinesia, and sputum culture guides therapy. Postural drainage and airway clearance devices clear secretions, antibiotics treat exacerbations, vaccines protect the lungs, and surgery is reserved for localised diseased lobes.
steps.say: Bronchiectasis causes a chronic wet cough in children. CT is showing dilated bronchi with thickened bronchial walls clearly. Sputum culture guides antibiotic choice during exacerbations. Airway clearance and vaccines protect the damaged lungs.

vis.alt: High-resolution CT scan of the lung showing characteristic features of bronchiectasis, including dilated bronchi (signet ring sign) and thickened bronchial walls (tramline sign), indicating chronic airway scarring.
vis.caption: Bronchiectasis: HRCT shows dilated, scarred airways with signet ring and tramline signs. Image: Avani R. Patel, Amar R. Patel, Shivank Singh, Shantanu Singh, Imran Kh, CC BY 3.0, Wikimedia Commons.

steps.tx: Control of asthma steps therapy up and down according to stability. Step up adds **long acting bronchodilator** combinations or montelukast, step down weans therapy when control is stable, and **severe disease** may need tiotropium or biologic referral. Adherence is checked by dose counters and refill history, inhaler technique is retrained, and rhinitis, reflux or obesity are treated alongside. Over reliance on reliever inhalers signals danger, steroid side effects are monitored, and adolescent self care is handed over gradually.
steps.say: Therapy steps up when asthma control remains poor. Therapy steps down when control stays stable over time. Clinicians check adherence and inhaler technique at every visit. Reliever overuse signals danger and needs urgent review.
